findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate T2's provider threshold as '>=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider' (dropping the undefined 'endpoint families' term) to match parent AC3 and the fuse-scope spec.
evidence: Parent AC3: 'provider fuse additionally requires >=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider'
Parent fuse-scope: 'no new "family" concept' and 'endpoint = one concrete provider instance ... the unit FailureScope.endpoint already denotes'
T2 AC2: 'Provider fuse additionally requires two endpoint families.'
T2 Plan step 2: 'Track provider scope only when failures span two endpoint families.'
container pairing: parent + 67d4-ecba-cf95-4353/d0ec-da23-32ba-47c6/dd65-54fa-f4c3-4bc9
findings.finding: T2 (dd65) states the provider-scope threshold as 'Provider fuse additionally requires two endpoint families' (AC2 and Plan step 2), but the parent AC3 and the parent's 'Fuse scope, eligibility & counter semantics' section define the requirement as '>=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider' and explicitly define 'endpoint' as one concrete provider instance with NO 'endpoint family' concept ('Grounded entirely in existing operation_outcome types — no new "family" concept'). 'Endpoint family' is undefined in the parent and in the fuse-scope spec, so T2 measures the criterion in different (and unspecified) terms.
scenarios: Two failing endpoints of the same provider: reviewer/implementer cannot tell whether 'endpoint families' means the parent's 'distinct endpoints of the same provider' or some coarser grouping, risking a fuse that opens on the wrong condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'two endpoint families' in T2 AC2 and Plan step 2 with 'two distinct endpoints of the same provider', matching the parent's FailureScope.endpoint/provider definitions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the 'of the same provider' constraint to T2's provider-threshold acceptance criterion.
evidence: Parent AC3: '>=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider'
T2 AC2: 'Provider fuse additionally requires two endpoint families.' (no same-provider constraint)
container pairing: parent + 67d4-ecba-cf95-4353/d0ec-da23-32ba-47c6/dd65-54fa-f4c3-4bc9
findings.finding: T2 (dd65) AC2 drops the 'of the same provider' qualifier that the parent AC3 attaches to the provider threshold. Parent AC3 requires the >=2 distinct endpoints to belong to the SAME provider; T2 AC2 states only 'two endpoint families' with no same-provider constraint, so the child, read as written, would open the provider fuse on two endpoints even if they belong to different providers.
scenarios: Two exhausted outcomes on endpoints belonging to two different providers: parent intent is that neither provider trips; T2's wording could trip a provider fuse spuriously.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend T2 AC2 to 'Provider fuse additionally requires two distinct endpoints of the same provider.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a child acceptance criterion asserting that verified-fake Cloud/DC batches show no premature termination of observed successful/partially successful work.
evidence: Parent AC6: 'Historical replay fixtures and verified-fake Cloud/DC batches show no premature termination of observed successful/partially successful work.'
T3 AC6: '...1,200-run slice shows zero premature stop before observed successful or partially successful work.' (replay only)
T3 AC2: 'Venue-gated Cloud/DC verified fakes pass before the coordinator default changes.' (a gate, not a no-premature-termination assertion)
No sibling AC (T1 d0ec, T2 dd65) asserts verified-fake Cloud/DC no-premature-termination.
container pairing: parent + 67d4-ecba-cf95-4353/d0ec-da23-32ba-47c6/dd65-54fa-f4c3-4bc9
findings.finding: Parent AC6 conjoins two observable proofs — 'Historical replay fixtures AND verified-fake Cloud/DC batches show no premature termination of observed successful/partially successful work.' T3 (67d4) AC6 delivers only the historical-replay half ('Historical replay of the completed 1,200-run slice shows zero premature stop'). No child acceptance criterion asserts that the verified-fake Cloud/DC batches specifically show no premature termination of observed successful/partial work: T3 AC2 asserts only that venue-gated verified fakes 'pass' before the default changes, and T3 AC4 asserts exact tallies/exit — neither states the 'no premature termination' outcome for the verified-fake batches. This half of AC6 is at most partially covered, with the uncovered remainder unnamed.
scenarios: A verified-fake Cloud/DC batch that prematurely stops an observed-successful op but still yields the expected tally/exit could pass T3's stated ACs while violating parent AC6's verified-fake half.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend T3 AC6 (or add an AC) so verified-fake Cloud/DC batches, not only the historical replay, assert no premature termination of observed successful/partial work.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-paragraph prior-art note naming the circuit-breaker pattern the new endpoint/provider fuse implements, citing the standard references (e.g. Azure Architecture Center / Wikipedia), and confirm the design's deviations (per-pass in-memory reset, no half-open probe state) are deliberate.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'Add a new endpoint-failure scoped fuse (none exists today).'

The design — 'Endpoint opens after 3 consecutive eligible outcomes across ≥2 tickets … A matching success resets consecutive state … Per-pass, in-memory, per-scope' — is the circuit-breaker state machine.

Retrieved prior art: Wikipedia 'Circuit breaker design pattern'; Azure Architecture Center 'Circuit Breaker Pattern'; the pattern's granular-scope guidance ('Use separate circuit breakers per endpoint, or at minimum, per distinct failure domain' — singhajit.com) directly matches the plan's per-endpoint/per-provider scoping.
The plan text nowhere contains the words 'circuit breaker', 'pybreaker', or 'resilience4j' (verified by reading the whole plan).
findings.finding: The plan introduces a 'new endpoint-failure scoped fuse' that is the classic circuit-breaker pattern (consecutive-failure threshold, open/reset states, granular scope, retry-inside-breaker) but never names that pattern or considers established prior art before committing to a bespoke design.
findings.location: Plan §'Fuse scope, eligibility & counter semantics'; Plan step 3; Outcome/Compatibility ('a new endpoint-failure scoped fuse')
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer needs to know whether this fuse is a well-understood pattern or a one-off; without naming it, the design cannot be checked against standard state semantics (e.g. a half-open probe state, which the plan omits).
Bug triage where the fuse trips unexpectedly and an operator reaches for standard circuit-breaker mental models.
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Fuse scope' section, state that the fuse is a per-scope circuit breaker, name the standard pattern, and note the intentional simplifications (per-pass zeroing instead of a timed half-open state; consecutive-failure + two-ticket/two-endpoint quorum) with the rationale grounded in the per-pass reconcile_once model.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify building a bespoke per-(provider,endpoint) fuse counter versus (a) an established breaker library such as pybreaker and (b) extending the existing classify.check_blast_radius / ADR 0028 breaker, stating why the eligibility semantics (budget-exhaustion provenance, per-pass reset) require a purpose-built implementation.
evidence: Repo already ships a circuit breaker: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/classify.py:305 check_blast_radius, wired via binding_walk.py:238 and documented in docs/adr/0028 / docs/adr/0027 ('The circuit breaker … is the …').

Plan distinguishes it: step 3 'The existing blast-radius mass-mutation guard (classify.check_blast_radius) is a distinct protection and is retained unchanged' — a defensible distinction, but the plan never weighs reuse/extension vs a second bespoke breaker.
Retrieved prior art: pybreaker (pypi.org/project/pybreaker) is a mature Python circuit-breaker implementation; the plan neither adopts nor rejects it with a reason.
No sentence in the plan gives a build-vs-reuse rationale for the new counter.
findings.finding: The plan chooses a bespoke hand-rolled per-(provider,endpoint) failure counter without evaluating whether an established breaker library (e.g. pybreaker) or an extension of the repo's existing circuit breaker (classify.check_blast_radius, ADR 0027/0028) could serve, so the anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three justification is missing.
findings.location: Plan §'Fuse scope … Counter durability/order'; Plan step 3 (blast-radius distinction)
scenarios: Maintenance divergence: two independently-evolved breakers (blast-radius + endpoint-fuse) in the same reconciler with different reset/scope semantics.
Adopting pybreaker later would require reworking the bespoke per-scope counters.
